content.text:
Done. All four behaviours are implemented with React's `<ViewTransition>` and Next's `transitionTypes`.

## What I found first

This project is on `next@16.3.1-canary.3`, where View Transitions are no longer experimental — worth knowing because the widely-documented approach doesn't apply:

- `experimental.viewTransition` **no longer exists** in Next's config schema, so I left `next.config.ts` untouched.
- Next aliases `react$` → its bundled React 19.3 canary, which exports `ViewTransition`/`addTransitionType` under **stable** names, not `unstable_*`. It's also in the `react-server` build, so `<ViewTransition>` works directly in Server Components — no `'use client'` needed anywhere.
- `next/link` accepts `transitionTypes?: string[]`, which Next passes to `addTransitionType` inside the navigation transition.

## Changes

**Shared element morph** (`ProductGrid.tsx`, `product/[slug]/page.tsx`) — thumbnail and hero share `name={`product-image-${slug}`}`, so they're captured as one group and the browser morphs position, size, and the 4:3 → 1:1 aspect change. Both carry `enter="none" exit="none"`, so the name is only active when a match exists — the three unmatched thumbnails keep no `view-transition-name`, stay inside the page snapshot, and slide out with the page instead of animating off on their own. In CSS the snapshots get `height: 100%; object-fit: fill` so the solid colour fills the morphing box rather than letterboxing.

**Directional page slide** (`layout.tsx`) — links pass `transitionTypes={['forward']}` (grid → detail) and `['back']` (back link); the root `<ViewTransition>` maps those to `vt-page-forward`/`vt-page-back`. The `default: 'none'` entry is deliberate: Suspense reveals bubble up to this boundary as an update, and without it every resolving skeleton would cross-fade the whole page.

**Suspense reveal** (`page.tsx`, detail page) — wrapping the boundary makes the fallback → children swap an update on one group, so skeleton cross-fades into content while the box eases between heights. `update="vt-reveal" enter="none" exit="none"` is exactly the shape React uses internally for Suspense boundaries (`getSuspenseViewTransition`), so it also drives the pre-hydration streaming reveal.

**Reduced motion** (`globals.css`) — `animation: none !important` on `::view-transition-group/image-pair/old/new(*)`. The wildcards and `!important` are needed to cancel the *user agent's* default cross-fade too, not just my keyframes; with nothing to wait for the transition completes on the next frame, giving a clean cut. The existing skeleton `pulse` is disabled in the same block.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` clean and `next build` green. I confirmed in the rendered output that the grid emits four unique `vt-name`s matching the detail page's (`product-image-leather-backpack` on both sides), that `transitionTypes: ["forward"]`/`["back"]` serialize to the client, and that the CSS survives minification with pseudo-element selectors and wildcards intact. I also read React's `commitEnter/ExitViewTransitions` and `getClassNameByType` to confirm `share` wins over `default` when paired and that `'none'` genuinely suppresses the name.

Two things to flag:

- **No browser was available in this sandbox**, so I verified the wiring statically and against React's commit code — I have not watched the animations run. Worth a click-through in Chrome.
- **I changed the detail page's outer `<div>` to `<main>`.** It previously rendered outside `main`, so it got none of the max-width or padding, making the page full-bleed and giving the page-slide group inconsistent geometry (1200px centred vs 100vw). That's a visible layout change beyond the animation work — revert that one tag if you want the old full-bleed detail page.

One behavioural note: browser back/forward buttons get no transition types from Next, so those navigations skip the page slide (the image still morphs). Adding a type there would need a popstate listener in a client component; I left it out as out of scope.
